about: What a chat's lines become as people use them (spec/chat.md). pins (Pins, Polls, Editing and unsending): a chat's `lines` by id in order, its `pins` the latest first, then one `step`: pin or unpin a line, unsend one (送信取消), or settle the poll a line carries (日にちを決める). `expected` is the pins after it, the latest first, and the one that made room for the new pin (`dropped`, for the app to say so), if any. The most pinned at once is design/src/chat.ts's chatRules.maxPins, 5. edited (Editing and unsending): a line with words and its link's page is given new words; `expected` says whether it keeps its page (`kept`) or takes the new words' (`new`). firstUnread (Unread lines and typing): who wrote each line, oldest first (`others`, `me`, or `app` for the app's own lines such as someone joining), and how many are unread; `expected` is the index of the line the chat opens on under ここから新着, null with nothing unread. Only others' lines count. directThread (One-to-one chats, spec/sync-protocol.md): two members' ids, given in either order; `expected` is their chat's thread id, the same from both sides: "direct:" and the two ids in order (by their UTF-16 code units, as every id is ASCII), joined by ":".

pins.name: a pinned line comes first among the pins
one pin past the most takes the place of the oldest
pinning a line already pinned only moves it up
taking a pin off leaves the others
a line taken back is not among the pins
a settled poll is pinned, within the most pins
settling a pinned poll again only moves its pin up

edited.name: an edit keeps its link's page while the link stays
a second link added after the first keeps the first's page
an edit that changes the link takes the new page
a new link put before the old one takes the new page
an edit that removes the link takes the new words' page, none

firstUnread.name: the chat opens on the first of the unread lines
the app's own lines and the reader's are not counted
with nothing unread there is no first unread line

directThread.name: the same chat from the other side
upper case orders before lower case
a shorter id that starts the other orders first
